clues.text: This person can summarize an entire crisis in one word: “Ominous.”
This person once opened an update with the calming phrase: “alright so here's some shit.”
This person's messages somehow end with “Thanks!” regardless of whether the request is tiny or terrifying.
If the message contains “Woo!! 💚”, there's a strong chance it came from this person.
This person once gave the team the extremely useful technical update: “I am going to ask Claude about this one.”
A request starts with “Quick change…”. This is usually the first sign of what?
A ticket has no AC, design is TBD, and launch is tomorrow. Naturally, it is ready for this meeting.
Product says frontend. Frontend says backend. Backend says Shopify. This is commonly known as…
The three most dangerous words in software: “Can we also…”
The sprint plan is best described as: A) a contract, B) a promise, C) a legally binding document, D) a suggestion
“Can confirm.” Translation: congratulations, the bug now has this.
“Is anyone else seeing this?” really means: please tell me this isn't just ______.
“Quick question.” This phrase guarantees absolutely nothing about the question's ______.
“Swarming on a fix.” Translation: several people's ______ have just been cancelled.
“Should be straightforward.” Finish the narrator voice: “It was _____ straightforward.”
In Good, Better, Best, this product is Good.
In Good, Better, Best, this product is Best.
Legal transformed AGZ Chocolate into this flavor name.
Essentials Gummies launched on the wonderfully inevitable internal holiday called ______.
This glamorous internal code name refers to the legacy AG1 formula still sold at Costco.
If you finish explaining a Sanity idea and discover a PR already exists, this person is a prime suspect.
If a Sanity component exists somewhere on the site, this designer probably has it documented in a spreadsheet.
If someone needs to confidently say “Ship it,” this Product leader is a strong candidate.
If something in #data-etl-alerts catches fire, tradition says this person gets tagged.
This person once built a whole custom Family Feud game and has now apparently decided one custom offsite game wasn't enough.
